project.name: guardog
project.description: Package security scanner for npm and PyPI that detects CVEs, reputation signals, malicious patterns, and threat intelligence without requiring AI or token services.

nodes.name: telegram-alert.js
nodes.summary: Delivers Telegram bot alerts when guard-dog detects dangerous packages. Formats rich alert messages from decision results and sends them via the Telegram Bot API.

nodes.name: decision-tree.js
nodes.summary: Evaluates scanner results through a scored decision tree to classify package risk as BARK, WHINE, or SILENT. Aggregates threat scores from VirusTotal, reputation, CVE, and pattern signals.

nodes.name: guard-dog.js
nodes.summary: Main orchestrator class that coordinates all scanners and produces a unified security verdict for a given package. Manages scan history, triggers Telegram alerts, and supports batch analysis.

nodes.name: cve-checker.js
nodes.summary: Queries the OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities) database for known CVEs affecting a package. Parses severity levels and calculates a threat score from the vulnerability counts.

nodes.name: pattern-analyzer.js
nodes.summary: Detects suspicious code patterns in package files using regex matching. Scores packages based on matched patterns associated with malicious behavior.

nodes.name: reputation-checker.js
nodes.summary: Checks package reputation across npm, PyPI, and RubyGems registries as well as GitHub. Aggregates download counts, stars, maintenance signals, and repository metadata into a reputation signal set.

nodes.name: threat-intel.js
nodes.summary: Aggregates threat intelligence from OSV, GitHub Security Advisories, NVD, and the CISA KEV catalog with disk-based caching. Provides per-package advisory lookup and cross-referencing against installed package lists.

nodes.name: virustotal-scanner.js
nodes.summary: Scans package URLs and file hashes against the VirusTotal v3 API for malware detection results. Returns parsed detection scores aggregated from multiple AV engine verdicts.

nodes.name: TelegramAlert
nodes.summary: Sends formatted Telegram bot messages when a dangerous package is detected. Handles message construction from decision results, alert dispatch, and connection testing.

nodes.name: DecisionTree
nodes.summary: Aggregates and weights scanner results into a final risk score and BARK/WHINE/SILENT verdict. Checks trusted provider allowlists and evaluates VirusTotal, reputation, CVE, and pattern subscores.

nodes.name: GuardDog
nodes.summary: Top-level coordinator that instantiates all scanners, runs them in sequence for a package, feeds results to the decision tree, persists scan history, and triggers Telegram alerts on BARK verdicts. Supports single and batch analysis modes.

nodes.name: CVEChecker
nodes.summary: Fetches CVE data from the OSV API for a named package and ecosystem. Parses severity from database metadata or CVSS scores and computes a weighted threat score.

nodes.name: PatternAnalyzer
nodes.summary: Applies regex-based suspicious pattern rules across package source files. Calculates a weighted score based on pattern category severity and match density.

nodes.name: ReputationChecker
nodes.summary: Multi-registry reputation aggregator querying npm, PyPI, RubyGems, and GitHub for package and repository metadata. Produces a list of positive and negative reputation signals consumed by the decision tree.

nodes.name: ThreatIntel
nodes.summary: Multi-source threat intelligence collector with disk-based caching. Queries OSV, GitHub Security Advisories, NVD, and the CISA KEV catalog, deduplicates findings by ID, and exposes efficient per-package advisory lookup.

nodes.name: VirusTotalScanner
nodes.summary: Wraps the VirusTotal v3 REST API to scan URLs and retrieve file hash reports. Parses AV engine detection statistics into a normalized result structure for the decision tree.

nodes.name: cve-checker.js
nodes.summary: Queries the OSV vulnerability database to check npm/PyPI packages for known CVEs and computes a numeric threat score from severity counts.

nodes.name: decision-tree.js
nodes.summary: Evaluates all security scan results through a weighted decision tree to produce a final risk score (SILENT/WHINE/BARK) and human-readable reasons.

nodes.summary: Claude Code agent instructions for the guard-dog agent. Defines the three verdict tiers (BARK >= 100, WHINE 50-99, SILENT < 50), the companion /gstack-cso code-level review skill, CLI entry points, and the nightly cron schedule.

nodes.name: CONTEXT.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative project context for Guardog. Describes it as a public npm/PyPI security scanner distributed to Mastermind students, covering the tech stack (Node.js ESM, better-sqlite3, dotenv), install URL, environment variables, CLI commands, verdict tiers, known issues, and key file inventory.

nodes.name: INDEX.md

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Primary public documentation for Guardog. Covers installation via npm (recommended), the setup wizard, all CLI commands (analyze, batch, doctor, install, updates, hooks), VirusTotal integration, the three verdicts (SILENT/WHINE/BARK), what checks are performed (CVE, reputation, code patterns, VirusTotal, threat cache), and cross-platform notes.

nodes.name: guardog.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code skill definition for the /guardog slash command. Instructs the agent to parse package name and ecosystem arguments, invoke the Node.js scanner, and report the verdict (SILENT/WHINE/BARK) with key reasons, an install recommendation, and a suggestion to run /gstack-cso for dangerous packages.

nodes.name: install.sh
nodes.summary: Legacy bash installer for Guardog (85 lines). Installs npm dependencies, creates the data directory, copies guardog.md to ~/.claude/skills/, optionally sets up a global git pre-commit hook, prompts for a VirusTotal API key, and then hands off to the Node.js setup wizard via src/index.js.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm package manifest for Guardog (guard-dog, v1.0.0, MIT). Declares src/index.js as both the main entry and the guardog/guard-dog CLI bin targets, defines scripts (start, test, scan, setup, cron), lists the published files set, specifies Node >= 18, and declares dotenv and node-fetch as runtime dependencies.

nodes.name: consolidate-logs.sh

nodes.name: git-precommit-hook.sh
nodes.summary: Git pre-commit hook that intercepts staged package.json changes, compares old versus new dependencies using git diff, and blocks the commit with exit code 1 if dangerous packages are detected.

nodes.name: npm-postinstall-hook.sh
nodes.summary: npm postinstall hook that automatically scans the current project's package.json after every npm install, propagating the scanner's exit code for dangerous packages but not blocking on network failures.

nodes.name: run-cso.sh
nodes.summary: Disabled stub that was intended to invoke the /gstack-cso code-level security review (OWASP Top 10 and STRIDE) after a guard-dog BARK or WHINE result; currently exits immediately with code 1 after Anthropic cleanup.

nodes.name: threat-intel-scan.sh

tour.title: What Guardog Does
tour.description: Guardog is a local package security scanner for npm and PyPI. It checks packages against CVE databases, reputation signals, code pattern analysis, and optional VirusTotal lookups before you install or commit dependencies. Every scan ends with one of three verdicts: SILENT (safe), WHINE (suspicious), or BARK (dangerous). Start here to understand what problem Guardog solves and what signals it uses.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: src/index.js is where all user-facing commands land. It exports the GuardDog class and wires up three subcommands: analyze (single package), batch (list from JSON), and doctor (system health). It also handles setup, git-hook management, and nightly-scan scheduling. Reading this file gives you the full map of what Guardog can do from the terminal.

tour.title: Verdict Scoring Thresholds
tour.description: All scanner results collapse into a single numeric score. config/config.json defines the cutoffs: BARK at 100 or above (danger, Telegram alert sent), WHINE between 50 and 99 (suspicious, warn user), and SILENT below 50 (safe). The CLAUDE.md skill doc captures these thresholds in compact form. Understanding the scoring system before reading individual scanners makes the weights make sense.

tour.title: CVE Database Lookup
tour.description: src/cve-checker.js queries the OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities) database for known CVEs affecting a package and version. It returns a list of advisories with severity levels that the decision tree converts into a threat score. This is the most straightforward scanner: a package name and ecosystem go in, a list of published vulnerabilities comes out.

tour.title: Reputation Signals
tour.description: src/reputation-checker.js fetches package metadata from npm, PyPI, RubyGems, and GitHub to build a reputation profile. Signals include download counts, maintainer count, time since last publish, whether a source repo exists, and open security issues. config/trusted-providers.json contains an allowlist of publishers whose packages skip detailed scanning to reduce false positives.

tour.title: Suspicious Code Patterns
tour.description: src/pattern-analyzer.js downloads the package tarball and scans its source files with a set of regex patterns that flag common malware techniques: base64 obfuscation, process spawning, network exfiltration calls, and credential harvesting. Each matched pattern contributes to the score with a configurable weight. This is the only scanner that actually reads package code rather than relying on external metadata.

tour.title: Threat Intelligence Aggregation
tour.description: src/threat-intel.js aggregates advisory data from OSV, GitHub Advisories, NVD (National Vulnerability Database), and CISA KEV (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog). Results are cached to disk to avoid redundant network calls. This scanner goes broader than cve-checker: it cross-references multiple authoritative threat feeds and flags packages with active exploitation evidence.

tour.title: VirusTotal Integration
tour.description: src/virustotal-scanner.js submits the package download URL or file hash to the VirusTotal v3 API and parses how many antivirus engines flagged it. This check is optional and requires an API key in .env. When a VirusTotal hit is returned, it carries heavy weight in the decision tree because multi-engine detection is a strong malware signal.

tour.title: Decision Tree Verdict
tour.description: src/decision-tree.js receives all scanner outputs and combines them into a total threat score using configurable weights. It first checks whether the publisher is on the trusted-providers allowlist and short-circuits if so. Otherwise it sums the CVE score, reputation score, pattern score, threat-intel score, and VirusTotal score, then maps the total to BARK, WHINE, or SILENT along with a reasons array explaining what drove the verdict.

tour.title: Operator Alerts
tour.description: src/telegram-alert.js formats and delivers a Telegram bot message whenever a scan verdict reaches BARK level. The message includes the package name, ecosystem, total threat score, and the list of reasons from the decision tree. This is the human-in-the-loop output: everything upstream is automated, and Telegram is where a dangerous finding surfaces to the operator.

tour.title: Developer Workflow Hooks
tour.description: bin/git-precommit-hook.sh blocks a git commit when staged package.json changes contain a package that returns BARK. bin/npm-postinstall-hook.sh runs an automatic scan after every npm install. These two scripts embed Guardog into the normal development workflow so dangerous packages are caught at the moment of introduction, without requiring the developer to remember to run a manual scan.

tour.title: Scheduled Automation
tour.description: bin/cron-nightly-scan.sh runs at 2:30 AM (GMT+8) and invokes bin/nightly-scan.js, which walks the filesystem to discover all package.json files and scans their dependencies. bin/threat-intel-scan.sh runs the threat intelligence refresh at 3:00 AM. Together these scripts keep threat data current and catch supply-chain attacks on packages that were safe when first installed.

tour.title: Setup and Path Resolution
tour.description: src/setup.js is the interactive setup wizard invoked by guardog setup. It persists user configuration, installs or removes the git pre-commit hook, and schedules or removes the nightly cron job. src/paths.js provides a single place where the tool resolves its home directory, data directory, config path, and .env path, making the rest of the codebase location-independent.
